_what: Per-question decisions for the January-2024 MES (AE/SDO) PHE General Studies import: keep-or-drop, GS syllabus unit and leaf sub-topic, and a one-line explanation of the keyed answer.
_split_policy: Static GK only, same rule as the other two sittings. `drop` marks a question whose answer decays - an office holder, an annual figure, a 'latest'/'as of 2023' framing. Every drop keeps its reason here and the importer prints them all on every run.
_this_paper_is_the_odd_one_out: Only 4 of 100 are dropped, against 21 for July-2023 and 7 for Oct-2025 - this paper is barely a current-affairs paper at all. What it has instead is two blocks the other two sittings do not: 28 reasoning and quantitative-aptitude questions (unit 10 is weighted 6 marks and this paper asks 28 of them), and an 11-question communication/management block that fits none of units 1-10. The second block is why GS unit 11 exists as of this import; see syllabus.js scope_revision_2026_09_05.
_new_leaves_used: Three questions sit on leaves added in this same change: Q14, Q17, Q48 and Q57 on unit 10's new 'Number system, divisibility, squares and cubes', and Q55, Q58, Q79 on 'Mensuration and coordinate geometry basics'. Both were added at no marks cost because such questions are routinely asked and previously had nowhere to sit - which is exactly why July-2023 Q82 had to be dropped. That drop is now reversible and should be revisited.
_key_quality: The strongest key of the three sittings. All 100 answers were checked independently and every quantitative one was worked by hand; not one is wrong. Two are contested and say so on the card. Q35 is DROPPED because the question is broken as printed rather than because the key is wrong: the worked example ZRYQ->KCJB is a shift of -15 but the keyed answer ELDK requires -11, so no single rule maps both, and this was confirmed by zooming the scan rather than assumed from OCR. Q15's keyed answer looks wrong on the merits and is kept with the dispute stated. Q51 is an ethics question whose key prefers surrendering at a police station over taking the victim to hospital; both are defensible and the card says so.

tags.reason: BROKEN AS PRINTED, not merely mis-keyed. The worked example ZRYQ -> KCJB is a uniform shift of -15 (Z-15=K, R-15=C, Y-15=J, Q-15=B), but the keyed answer ELDK requires -11 from PWOV (P-11=E, W-11=L, O-11=D, V-11=K). No single rule produces both, and applying the example's own -15 to PWOV gives AHZG, which is not offered. Confirmed by zooming the scan rather than trusting OCR, so this is the Commission's misprint and not extraction damage. Importing it would teach a pattern that does not exist.

tags.exp: P+B-R×Q. Read it left to right: P+B makes P the son of B; B-R makes B the husband of R, so R is P's mother; R×Q makes R the sister of Q. Q is therefore the brother of P's mother - the maternal uncle.
